Una ecuación $y′ = f(x, y)$ da en cada p: An equation $y′ = f(x, y)$ gives at each point of the plane the slope of the solution passing through it. By drawing those slopes you see the shape of all the solutions without solving anything. Euler's method advances in steps of size h following the slope:
$y_{n+1} = y_n + h f(x_n, y_n)$, &ensp;: $y_{n+1} = y_n + h f(x_n, y_n)$,   $x_{n+1} = x_n + h$
Su error al final es proporcional a h: c: Its final error is proportional to h: with half the step, roughly half the error. Heun (improved Euler) and the midpoint method use two slopes per step and their error goes as h²; fourth-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) uses four and its error goes as h⁴. The comparison table shows it: when h is halved, the error is divided by about 2, 4 or 16.
